```{r loadResults, include=FALSE}
# HTML image labels for ggtext strip rendering

stimPngDir <- "../figures_and_schematics/legend_icons/stimulus_pair_icons"

natcanImgLabels <- c(

  "Canopy F"  = paste0("<img src='", stimPngDir, "/canopyF.png' width='", imgW, "'/><br/>**Canopy F**"),
  "Canopy G1" = paste0("<img src='", stimPngDir, "/canopyG.png' width='", imgW, "'/><br/>**Canopy G1**"),

)

artImgLabels <- setNames(

    paste0("<img src='", stimPngDir, "/perpPara.png' width='",    imgW, "'/><br/>**Perp./Para.**"),
    paste0("<img src='", stimPngDir, "/thickOb.png' width='",     imgW, "'/><br/>**Thick oblique**"),

```

Evidence that wasps can use overhead patterns to navigate comes from two observations. First, that the proportion of choices for the rewarding pattern $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is >50% and second, that this proportion drops when the patterns are removed from the ceiling (during the control). We begin by asking whether wasps can discriminate stimulus patterns consisting of black stripes oriented perpendicularly to each other on the first-chamber ceilings of the two Y-maze arms (for stimulus conditions, see Figure 2A).

# Can wasps discriminate 'simple' artificial dorsal patterns?

For the test phase of the perpendicular-parallel artificial stimulus pair, trial number had a significant positive effect on $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ (@fig-q2, solid line;
p`r mAllCoefsRef["perpPara_170725", "rank_trial_pFmt"]`), with $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ rising from
`r emmPtsRef["perpPara_170725", "first_prob"]`% (95% CI `r emmPtsRef["perpPara_170725", "first_confint"]`) at trial 1 to `r emmPtsRef["perpPara_170725", "last_test_prob"]`% (95% CI
`r emmPtsRef["perpPara_170725", "last_test_confint"]`) by test end (@tbl-overview), which was significantly above chance (lower 95% CI bound \>50%; @fig-q2 test panel).

Additionally a Wald z-test revealed end-of-test $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ was significantly higher than at the start of the control phase (`r emmPtsRef["perpPara_170725", "ctrl_start_prob"]`%, 95% CI
`r emmPtsRef["perpPara_170725", "ctrl_start_confint"]`; @fig-q2) with the log-odds ratio between these points significantly greater than 0 (p`r contrastsRef["perpPara_170725", "pFmt"]`).

Also note that $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is significantly above chance from an early trial number (grey
shaded 95% confidence ribbon in @fig-q2 does not overlap the 50% line) and remains that way until the end of the test.
In contrast, the $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ in the control phase is never
significantly above chance for the duration of the control (95%
confidence ribbon overlaps the 50% line), as one would expect for wasps
making choices in the absence of any information regarding the location
of the reward.

That the model suggests naive wasps nearly perform significantly above
chance at the onset of the test phase (ie. in trial 1) is possibly due
to the model being unable to fit the rapid learning of the wasps, rather
than to the wasps having learned olfactory / temporal cues during the
pre-test training phase that persisted into the test. This is supported
by the proportion of correct decisions in the first few 3-trial wide
windows of the test phase (grey points, @fig-q2) that are clustered around 50%.

# What information are wasps using to discriminate patterns?

```{r fig-q2}
#| fig-cap: 'Wasp reward-navigation performance for artificial stimulus experiments. Each row shows one experiment with a particular pair of stimuli (stimulus conditions as in Figure 2A-D); columns show test and, when run, control phases per experiment. During the test phase, overhead artificial stimuli could be used by the wasps to choose the rewarding chamber, but during the control phase, when these stimuli were removed, performance dropped to chance levels. The y-axis represents the probability of a wasp entering (or "choosing") the second arm chamber that contained the reward (constituting a "correct choice"). The solid black line shows the predicted probability of correct choices across trials and the grey ribbon the 95% confidence interval around these probabilities given by the models. Grey points are the proportion (not the probability) of correct choices made by all wasps in 3-trial wide rolling windows. Black points represent the predicted probabilities of correct choices at the end of the test and the start of the control phases, and the error bars the 95% confidence intervals around these predictions. The dashed horizontal line represents chance performance (50%). Only the first choice of each wasp in each trial was used as data in the model and to calculate the rolling means.'
#| fig-height: 5

q2ExpOrder <- c("perpPara_170725", "thinOb_150823", "thickOb_140823", "brightDiff_250725")

emmAllArt <- emmAll %>%
  filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder) %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(artLabels[q2ExpOrder])),
    manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))
  )

p <- ggplot(emmAllArt, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "Probability of correct choice (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_grid(experiment ~ manipulation, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(experiment = as_labeller(artImgLabels))) +
  theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(1, "lines"),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y.right = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0)
)

rollingArt <- choices_rolling %>%
  filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder) %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(artLabels[q2ExpOrder])),
    manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))
  )

p <- p + geom_point(data = rollingArt, aes(x = rank_trial, y = pcorr),
                    colour = "black", alpha = 0.1)

emmPtsArt <- emmPts %>%
  filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder,
         trial_pos %in% c("last_test", "ctrl_start")) %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(artLabels[q2ExpOrder]))
  )

p <- p +
  geom_errorbar(data = emmPtsArt,
                aes(x = rank_trial, ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL),
                width = 2) +
  geom_point(data = emmPtsArt, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob))

p <- p +
  geom_text(
    data = nLabels %>%
      filter(experiment %in% q2ExpOrder) %>%
      mutate(
        experiment   = recode(experiment, !!!artLabels),
        experiment   = factor(experiment, levels = unname(artLabels[q2ExpOrder])),
        manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))
      ),
    aes(label = label),
    x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.3,
    size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  )

print(p)
rm(q2ExpOrder, emmAllArt, rollingArt, emmPtsArt, p)
```

```{r q2ContrastArtStimuli}
q2TrialSlopeTable <- allTrialSlopeRef %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "artificial") %>%
  select(-nat_or_art)

```

In the previous experiment (@fig-q2, top), wasps may have located the rewarding arm by using the different extents of optic flow encountered when flying under the parallel and perpendicular stripes (respectively the left and right panels of Figure 2A), rather than the patterns themselves. 
Wasps would experience little optic flow with parallel stipes, and considerable optic flow with perpendicular stripes. 
To determine whether wasps used optic flow, we next used oblique stripes oriented at either 45° to the right or 45° to the left of the Y-maze arm’s long axis and the general direction of wasp travel (for stimulus conditions, see Figure 2B,C).
Even though these two patterns clearly differ, they will present identical optic flow in the front to back direction for wasps flying beneath them.
Here again, we look for $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ \>50% and a larger $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the end of the test relative to the start of the control as evidence that wasps can distinguish stimuli that generate identical rates of optic flow.

Wasps had no trouble distinguishing between oblique stripes that produce identical rates of front to back optic flow in the dorsal visual field (@fig-q2, row two and three). 
For the thin oblique stripe condition (Figure 2B), trial had a significant positive effect on
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ (p`r q2TrialSlopeTable["thinOb_150823", "pFmt"]`; @tbl-model-coefs),
with performance rising from `r emmPtsRef["thinOb_150823", "first_prob"]`% (95% CI `r emmPtsRef["thinOb_150823", "first_confint"]`) at trial 1 to `r emmPtsRef["thinOb_150823", "last_test_prob"]`% (95% CI `r emmPtsRef["thinOb_150823", "last_test_confint"]`) by test end --- significantly above chance (50%). $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at test end was also significantly above performance at the start of the control phase (`r emmPtsRef["thinOb_150823", "ctrl_start_prob"]`%, 95% CI `r emmPtsRef["thinOb_150823", "ctrl_start_confint"]`; p`r contrastsRef["thinOb_150823","pFmt"]`). Again, the  $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ in the control phase was never significantly above chance for the duration of the control (95% confidence ribbon overlaps the 50% line),

For the thick oblique experiment (Figure 2C), trial had a positive but non-significant effect on
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ (p = `r q2TrialSlopeTable["thickOb_140823", "pFmt"]`; @tbl-model-coefs),
with performance rising from `r emmPtsRef["thickOb_140823", "first_prob"]`%
to `r emmPtsRef["thickOb_140823", "last_test_prob"]`% by test end ---
also significantly above chance. 

Next, we asked whether wasps could discriminate between an opaque and
transparent ceiling, ie. between stimuli that carried little to no pattern
information but with clear differences in brightness (stimulus condition as in Figure 2C). 
Trial had a positive but non-significant effect on $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ (p = `r q2TrialSlopeTable["brightDiff_250725", "pFmt"]`; @tbl-model-coefs),
likely due to the shorter number of trials run in this experiment, and
performance rose from `r emmPtsRef["brightDiff_250725", "first_prob"]`%
(95% CI `r emmPtsRef["brightDiff_250725", "first_confint"]`) at trial 1 to
`r emmPtsRef["brightDiff_250725", "last_test_prob"]`% (95% CI
`r emmPtsRef["brightDiff_250725", "last_test_confint"]`) by test end.
While performance at the end of the experiment is only borderline
significantly higher than 50%, this is likely an artifact of the
increased uncertainty in the slope / effect of trial number on
performance due to the lower number of trials run in this experiment. 
If one for example looks at the middle trials (@tbl-overview), the lower bound of
performance is considerably higher than chance.

# Can wasps use naturalistic patterns for navigation?

```{r fig-q3-tc}
#| fig-cap: 'Wasp reward-navigation performance for six naturalistic stimulus experiments. Each row shows wasp performance over two phases (columns, test and control) of an experiment. In the test phase a pair of naturalistic stimuli (at right) were displayed from above in a Y-maze, with one of the stimuli in the pair associated with a reward and the other with no reward (see Methods for further details). During the control phase the stimuli were removed but the reward remained in place. Not all experiments had a control phase (blank panels). Note that performance is only significantly above chance for some stimulus pairs / experiments, and that predicted performance at the end of the test is rarely significantly higher than at the start of the control. All other figure conventions as in Figure 3.'
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-pos: "p"

emmAllNat <- emmAll %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic", experiment != "natcan3_080825") %>%
  droplevels() %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))
emmPtsNat <- emmPts %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic", experiment != "natcan3_080825",
         trial_pos %in% c("last_test", "ctrl_start")) %>%
  droplevels() %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))
tbNatTcPts  <- emmPtsRef %>% filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic",
                                     rownames(.) != "natcan3_080825")

rollingNat <- choices_rolling %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic", experiment != "natcan3_080825") %>%
  droplevels() %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))

p <- ggplot(emmAllNat, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL),
    alpha = 0.15,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(experiment ~ manipulation, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(experiment = as_labeller(natcanImgLabels))) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "Probability of correct choice (%)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.spacing.y = unit(0.75, "lines"),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.text.y.right = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0),
        strip.background = element_blank())

p <- p + geom_point(data = rollingNat, aes(x = rank_trial, y = pcorr),
                    colour = "black", alpha = 0.1)

p <- p +
  geom_errorbar(data = emmPtsNat,
                aes(x = rank_trial, ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL),
                width = 2) +
  geom_point(data = emmPtsNat, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob))

p <- p +
  geom_text(
    data = nLabels %>%
      filter(experiment %in% names(natcanLabels), experiment != "natcan3_080825") %>%
      mutate(
        experiment   = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels),
        manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))
      ),
    aes(label = label),
    x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.3,
    size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  )

print(p)
rm(emmAllNat, emmPtsNat, tbNatTcPts, rollingNat, p)
```

Evidence for whether wasps can discriminate naturalistic canopies (see Figure 2 D-I) at
above-chance rates (\>50%) is mixed. 
In three of the six naturalistic canopy pairs we tested, the predicted $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ by the end of the test was significantly (canopy E, G2) or borderline significantly (canopy I) above chance (the lower limit of the 95% CI is \>50%; @fig-q3-tc, @tbl-overview, @fig-supp-canopyG1), but for the other three canopy pairs this was not the case. 
This suggests that wasps may be able to separate certain pairs of naturalistic canopies, although the performance is generally lower than for artificial stimuli (see below).

For two of the three naturalistic canopies that show a $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ significantly or near significantly greater than 50%, after two of those we also ran a control (patterns removed) directly
after the test phase concluded, but in only one case (Canopy E) was the $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the end of the test significantly higher than at the start of the control. 
This can be attributed to the fact that $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ for the naturalistic canopies is generally not much greater than 50% (if at all), and the fact that control experiments were
not run for many trials, increasing the uncertainty around the $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ at the start of the control phase.

# Performance differences among naturalistic and artificial stimuli

```{r fig-q3-natart}
#| fig-cap: "End-of-test predicted performance by canopy type."

q3NatArtEndPts <- emmPts %>%
  filter(trial_pos == "last_test") %>%
  mutate(
    nat_or_art = factor(nat_or_art, levels = c("naturalistic", "artificial"))
  )

natArtMean <- q3NatArtEndPts %>%
  group_by(nat_or_art) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_prob = mean(prob),
    min_prob  = min(prob),
    max_prob  = max(prob),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = nat_or_art,
    values_from = c(mean_prob, min_prob, max_prob),
    names_glue  = "{nat_or_art}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  mutate(diff_mean_prob = artificial_mean_prob - naturalistic_mean_prob) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_prob"), ~as.character(as.integer(round(. * 100)))))

q3NatBest  <- q3NatArtEndPts %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic") %>%
  slice_max(order_by = prob, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(prob  = as.character(as.integer(round(prob * 100))),
         label = unname(natcanLabels[experiment]))

q3ArtWorst <- q3NatArtEndPts %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "artificial") %>%
  slice_min(order_by = prob, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(prob  = as.character(as.integer(round(prob * 100))),
         label = unname(artLabels[experiment]))

ptJitter   <- position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 3)
canopyCols <- c(naturalistic = "forestgreen", artificial = "black")
rm(q3NatArtEndPts, ptJitter)
```

Discrimination performance for naturalistic canopies tends to be lower
than for artificial canopies (@fig-q3-combined).
The naturalistic canopy showing the best performance (`r q3NatBest$label`, $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ =
`r q3NatBest$prob`%) still has a lower $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ than the
artificial canopy with the worst performance (Transparent/Opaque,
$P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ = `r q3ArtWorst$prob`%).
The average performance for all naturalistic canopies is `r natArtMean$naturalistic_mean_prob`%,
whereas for artificial stimuli it is `r natArtMean$artificial_mean_prob`%, and the difference in the average $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ for naturalistic and artificial stimuli is `r natArtMean$diff_mean_prob`%. Given the low number of artificial and naturalistic experiments included here (n = 4 and 7 respectively) we did not test for an overall difference between naturalistic and artificial canopies.

Additionally, the effects of trial on $P_{\mathrm{corr}}$ were modest for naturalistic stimuli in comparison to artificial stimuli (compare trial coefficients in @tbl-model-coefs) and were only significantly greater than zero for canopy G2. This translated to small performance increases between trial 1 and trial 26 for naturalistic stimuli relative to artificial stimuli (@tbl-overview).

```{r fig-q3-combined}
#| fig-cap: "Probability of correct choices for naturalistic and artificial experiments at the maximum common test-phase trial across experiments. A. Probability of a correct choice across all experiments in the same plot (best fit lines) and 95% confidence intervals around those probailities (shaded ribbons). The points in A show the predicted probability of a correct choice at trial 26, the maximum test-phase trial that is common to all experiments. B. The performance at trial 26 compared between artificial and naturalistic experiments. Points in B are the same as those in A."

library(patchwork)

# Per-experiment colour mapping: black for artificial, green for naturalistic
allExpLabels <- c(artLabels, natcanLabels)
expCols <- c(
  setNames(rep("black",       length(artLabels)),    unname(artLabels)),
  setNames(rep("forestgreen", length(natcanLabels)), unname(natcanLabels))
)

# Test-phase prediction curves for all experiments
allExpTestAll <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test") %>%
  mutate(experiment = dplyr::recode(experiment, !!!allExpLabels))

# Maximum shared trial: highest trial number reached by every experiment
maxSharedTrial <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test") %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(max_trial = max(rank_trial), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(max_trial) %>%
  min()

# Predicted point at the shared trial for each experiment
emmSharedPt <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test", rank_trial == maxSharedTrial) %>%
  mutate(experiment = dplyr::recode(experiment, !!!allExpLabels))

# Panel A: overlaid learning curves
pA <- ggplot(allExpTestAll,
             aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob,
                 group = experiment, colour = experiment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL, fill = experiment),
              colour = NA, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = emmSharedPt, size = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = expCols, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = expCols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100, limits = c(0.25, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "Probability of correct choice (%)") +
  theme_bw()

# Panel B: jittered points at the shared trial reference point
pB <- ggplot(emmSharedPt, aes(x = nat_or_art, y = prob)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(color = nat_or_art), size = 2, alpha = 0.7,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 3)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = canopyCols,
                     labels = c(artificial = "Artificial", naturalistic = "Naturalistic")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100, limits = c(0.25, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Stimulus type", y = "Probability of correct choice (%) \nat trial 26", color = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A"))
rm(allExpLabels, expCols, allExpTestAll, maxSharedTrial, emmSharedPt, pA, pB)
```

```{r supplementaryTbls}
roundNumsInString <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  vapply(
    x,
    function(s) {
      nums <- regmatches(s, gregexpr("-?[0-9]+\\.?[0-9]*", s, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
      if (length(nums) == 0) return(s)
      out     <- s
      rounded <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), as.numeric(nums))
      for (i in seq_along(nums)) out <- sub(nums[i], rounded[i], out, fixed = TRUE)
      out
    },
    character(1)
  )
}
```

```{r tbl-overview}
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted $P_{\\mathrm{corr}}$ at key trial positions and test--control contrasts for all experiments. Control start and contrast columns are blank for test-only experiments."
#| eval: !expr knitr::pandoc_to() != "docx"

expOrder <- c(q2ArtTableOrder, names(natcanLabels))

# Prediction at the maximum shared test trial across all experiments
sharedTrial <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test") %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(max_trial = max(rank_trial), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(max_trial) %>%
  min()

sharedPtTbl <- emmAll %>%
  filter(manipulation == "test", rank_trial == sharedTrial) %>%
  mutate(sharedPcorr95CI = paste0(
    as.integer(round(prob * 100)), "% [",
    as.integer(round(asymp.LCL * 100)), ", ",
    as.integer(round(asymp.UCL * 100)), "]"
  )) %>%
  select(experiment, sharedPcorr95CI)

allExpOverview <- emmPtsTbl %>%
  left_join(sharedPtTbl, by = "experiment") %>%
  left_join(
    contrastsTbl %>% select(experiment, logOddsRatio95CI, pFmt),
    by = "experiment"
  ) %>%
  left_join(nSummary, by = "experiment") %>%
  mutate(experiment = factor(experiment, levels = expOrder)) %>%
  arrange(experiment) %>%
  mutate(experiment = dplyr::recode(as.character(experiment), !!!c(artLabels, natcanLabels)))

n_art    <- sum(allExpOverview$nat_or_art == "artificial")
n_nat    <- sum(allExpOverview$nat_or_art == "naturalistic")

tbl <- allExpOverview %>%
  select(experiment, firstPcorr95CI, midPcorr95CI, lastTestPcorr95CI,
         sharedPcorr95CI, ctrlStartPcorr95CI, logOddsRatio95CI, pFmt) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ if_else(is.na(.), "---", .))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Experiment", "Test start", "Test middle", "Test end",
                  paste0("Trial ", sharedTrial), "Control start",
                  "Log-odds ratio [95% CI]", "P"),
    booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::add_header_above(
    c(" " = 1, "$P_{\\\\mathrm{corr}}$ [95\\\\% CI]" = 5, " " = 2),
    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("Artificial", 1, n_art) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("Naturalistic", n_art + 1, n_art + n_nat) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9, latex_options = "hold_position")

# knitr::kable converts non-ASCII chars to <U+XXXX> sequences; fix them here
# after all kableExtra processing (which would re-escape LaTeX backslashes)
knitr::asis_output(
  gsub("<U\\+00B0>", "$^{\\\\circ}$",
  gsub("<U\\+00B1>", "$\\\\pm$",
  gsub("<U\\+2014>", "---",
  gsub("< ", "$<$ ",
       paste(as.character(tbl), collapse = "\n")))))
)
rm(expOrder, sharedTrial, sharedPtTbl, tbl)
```

```{r tbl-sample-sizes}
#| tbl-cap: "Per-experiment sample sizes and test-phase duration. Wasps and choices are split by phase (test and control). Last trial is the highest trial number reached in the test phase. Control columns are blank for test-only experiments."
#| eval: !expr knitr::pandoc_to() != "docx"

)
```

```{r supp-model-table-prep}
#| include: false
suppArtModelData <- mAllCoefsTbl %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "artificial") %>%
  mutate(experiment = forcats::fct_relevel(experiment, q2ArtTableOrder)) %>%
  arrange(experiment, term)

suppNatModelData <- mAllCoefsTbl %>%
  filter(nat_or_art == "naturalistic") %>%
  mutate(
    experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels),
    experiment = factor(experiment, levels = unname(natcanLabels))
  ) %>%
  arrange(experiment, term)

suppModelData <- bind_rows(suppArtModelData, suppNatModelData)

# Group anchors for pack_rows — art block
suppArtModelGroups <- suppArtModelData %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    end   = cumsum(n),
    start = end - n + 1,
    label = unname(artLabels[as.character(experiment)])
  )

# Group anchors for pack_rows — nat block (row indices continue after art block)
artNRows <- nrow(suppArtModelData)
suppNatModelGroups <- suppNatModelData %>%
  group_by(experiment) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    end   = artNRows + cumsum(n),
    start = end - n + 1,
    label = as.character(experiment)
  )

suppModelTable <- suppModelData %>%
  select(term, logOdds95CI, pFmt)
```

```{r tbl-model-coefs}
#| tbl-cap: "Model coefficients for all experiments. Fixed effects: trial number, side alternation, reward side, and (for experiments with a control phase) experiment phase (manipulation) and its interaction with trial number. Random effect: individual ID."
#| eval: !expr knitr::pandoc_to() != "docx"
k <- knitr::kable(
  suppModelTable,
  col.names = c("Term", "Log-odds [95% CI]", "P"),
  booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE
)
allGroups <- bind_rows(suppArtModelGroups, suppNatModelGroups)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(allGroups))) {
  k <- kableExtra::pack_rows(k,
    allGroups$label[i],
    allGroups$start[i],
    allGroups$end[i]
  )
}
knitr::asis_output(
  gsub("<U\\+2014>", "---",
  gsub("< ", "$<$ ",
       paste(as.character(k), collapse = "\n")))
)
rm(k, allGroups)
```

## Additional experiments

```{r fig-supp-experiments}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Wasp performance for two additional \"control\" experiments not included in the main analysis. A. In this experiment we first tested whether a group of wasps could discriminate a naturalistic pair of stimuli (left panel, same data as presented in @{fig-q3-tc} row 6). To rule out that performance differences between naturalistic and artificial stimuli might be driven by differences in wasp species, hives, individuals or phase of the season, we tested if the same group of wasps could discriminate the perpendicular-parallel artificial stimuli (right panel) immediately following a naturalistic canopy stimulus pair (left panel). Note that the same wasp individuals that could not discriminate the naturalistic stimuli can discriminate the artificial stimuli. B. To rule out the possibility that above-chance discrimination of dorsal stimuli might be explained by the use of reflections of the dorsal stimuli off surfaces of the Y-maze that are ventral or lateral to the wasps (i.e. the bottom and sides of the maze) we covered first the bottom (middle panel) and then the sides of the maze (right panel) with LEE Filter 1/4 white diffuser film (251). Note that performance remains well above chance after the addition of diffuser paper."
#|
```

## Canopy G1

```{r fig-supp-canopyG1}
#| fig-cap: "Wasp reward-navigation performance for the Canopy G1 naturalistic stimulus experiment. This was a \"pilot\" canopy experiment that we later repeated with an increased number of trials (canopy G2 in @{fig-q3-tc}). The panels show wasp performance over the test and control phases of the experiment. All other figure conventions as in @fig-q3-tc."
#| fig-height: 2

g1ID <- "natcan3_080825"

emmG1All <- emmAll %>%
  filter(experiment == g1ID) %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))
emmG1Pts <- emmPts %>%
  filter(experiment == g1ID, trial_pos %in% c("last_test", "ctrl_start")) %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))
rollG1 <- choices_rolling %>%
  filter(experiment == g1ID) %>%
  mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels))

pG1 <- ggplot(emmG1All, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) x * 100, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = rollG1, aes(x = rank_trial, y = pcorr), colour = "black", alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_errorbar(data = emmG1Pts, aes(x = rank_trial, ymin = asymp.LCL, ymax = asymp.UCL), width = 2) +
  geom_point(data = emmG1Pts, aes(x = rank_trial, y = prob)) +
  geom_text(
    data = nLabels %>%
      filter(experiment == g1ID) %>%
      mutate(experiment = recode(experiment, !!!natcanLabels),
             manipulation = factor(manipulation, levels = c("test", "control"))),
    aes(label = label),
    x = Inf, y = -Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_grid(experiment ~ manipulation, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = labeller(experiment = as_labeller(natcanImgLabels))) +
  labs(x = "Trial", y = "Probability of correct choice (%)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),
        strip.text.y.right = ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 0),
        strip.background = element_blank())

print(pG1)
rm(g1ID, emmG1All, emmG1Pts, rollG1, pG1)
```
